notes: Access tier 1 (direct HTTP fetch, no browser needed) - robots.txt (https://www.royaldesign.com/robots.txt) is 'User-agent: * / Allow: /', no Claude-specific disallow. Site is server-rendered React/Vike; each PLP embeds its own facet/pagination state as inline JSON with an exact 'totalProducts' field (structured-data qty source, priority 2), used throughout instead of any capped/estimated figure. Storefront checked is the US store (/us/), confirmed English. Discovered the seasonal tree by combining the /us/ mega-menu, the /us/christmas hub page's own sub-nav, each child page's further sub-nav (3 levels deep in places), and the full page-sitemap (https://royaldesign.com/us/sitemap_pages_0.xml, 4.2MB, every URL on the US store) grepped for christmas/xmas/easter/valentine/halloween/diwali/thanksgiving/holi/rakhi/eid/new-year - this sitemap sweep is the absence proof for Halloween, Diwali, Thanksgiving, Eid, Holi/Rakhi and New Year as categories: zero matching URLs anywhere on the site (all locales), not just a search-based null result. Internal site search (/us/search?q=...) was tried as a secondary check but is non-discriminating - halloween/diwali/thanksgiving all returned the identical sitewide total (17,890), the known false-absence trap, so it was not relied on; the sitemap sweep is the real evidence. RoyalDesign, despite being a large Scandinavian retailer, has a comparatively narrow seasonal taxonomy limited to Christmas (extensive, multi-level) and one Easter category - no Diwali/Halloween/Thanksgiving/Indian-festival categories exist. CHRISTMAS: root hub /us/christmas (own totalProducts 310) breaks into 4 branches whose own totals sum to 311 (310 vs 311, one-product rounding/overlap, not a material mismatch) - kept as a grouping row over its branches, never double-counted against them. 'Christmas Decorations & Ornaments' (/us/christmas/christmas-decorations, totalProducts 148) further subdivides into 7 real sub-pages summing to 156 (148 vs 156, modest facet overlap expected per the overlap rule) - kept as a grouping row over its children; one of the 7 children, 'Angel Chimes & Christmas Angels' (/us/christmas/christmas-decorations/angel-chimes-christmas-angels), showed totalProducts 0 and was dropped as an empty category rather than written as a zero row. 'Christmas Lights' (/us/christmas/christmas-lights, totalProducts 89) subdivides into exactly 2 children whose totals sum to exactly 89 (21+68) - kept as a grouping row. 'Christmas Table Settings' (/us/christmas/christmas-table-settings, totalProducts 51) subdivides into exactly 5 children summing to exactly 51 (7+9+11+10+14) - kept as a grouping row. 'Christmas Textiles' (/us/christmas/christmas-textiles, totalProducts 23) subdivides into exactly 2 children summing to exactly 23 (13+10) - kept as a grouping row. The two 'advent candle holder' pages (one filed under Christmas Decorations, one filed under Christmas Lights, both totalProducts 21) are different URLs with different sampled product IDs (no overlap in the visible product-ID sample), not the same listing under two names, so both are kept per the coexistence rule rather than deduplicated. EASTER: only one genuine seasonal category exists, 'Easter Decorations' (/us/home-dcor/decorations/easter-decorations, totalProducts 81, a sibling of ordinary Home Decor sub-categories like vases/sculptures, not part of a larger Easter branch) - recorded as a single leaf row with no grouping parent needed. EXCLUDED as marketing/navigation, not product categories (no 'totalProducts' or product grid present on any of them, confirmed by direct fetch): /us/season/christmas, /us/season/easter, /us/season/valentines-day, /us/season/black-friday, /us/season/cyber-monday, /us/season/singles-day, /us/season/gift-ideas (all CMS campaign-hub pages linking out to the real category pages above plus inspiration/blog content); /us/christmas-shop and /us/valentines-day (same landing-page template, no product grid - 'Valentine's Day' has no genuine PLP anywhere on the site, only these two marketing pages and a /us/campaign/valentines-day promo, so it is correctly absent from rows, not just under-covered); every /us/campaign/* URL (christmas, christmas-deals, christmas-decor, christmas-gift-ideas, easter-offer, holiday-sale, tablesetting-for-new-year, valentines-day, valentines-weekend, etc. - promotional pages); every /us/inspiration/* URL (christmas-inspiration, christmas gift guides, easter style-tips - editorial); every /us/series/* URL (house-doctor-christmas, dbkd-easter, moomin-arabia-festive-moments, spiegelau-festival, spode-christmas-tree - brand/product-line pages, not categories, per the shared core's brand-page exclusion). No PDP crawling was used at any point; all classification came from hub/PLP pages and their own embedded facet state.
